text:
Whether you traffic forged pardons, cheat at dice, or counterfeit current coins like those who end scalded,* godless criminal and bandit, whether you swindle, rob, or commit adultery, where ends your ill-gotten gold? All goes to taverns and women.

Rhyme, mock, play an instrument like fools protected by disguise; turn clown or magician, invent a tale, stage mockeries, farces, and moralities wherever allowed, win at cards: all you acquire—listen and do not be angry—all goes to taverns and women.

Do such infamies repel you? Then plow fields and meadows, curry horses, asses, and mules if you are not learned, and you will earn enough. But if you are one of those who crush hemp, is it not true that the product of your arm all goes to taverns and women?

Hose, doublets, breeches, cloak, and every garment you have—take them, hurry, age escapes!—quickly to taverns, to women.


* “Scalded” refers to counterfeiters, for unauthorized coiners were put to death that way.

translation.title: Ballad of Good Doctrine
